extends: experiments/2026-09-10_03_cand_microbench -- same instrument (cmd/candbench), same empty-snapshot methodology, same hot-cell derivation (-hot-k 6), same -recall-k 12 reference. This experiment re-reads _03's per-family TSVs and adds the -global-k A/B.
question: User asked: (1) can the probability that the candidate-selection scheme fails to include the optimum be quantified -- give a number; (2) what are the suggestions for improving candidate quality.
answer_summary: Quantified at the only layer that is measurable with a singleton reference (L1: the best single-waypoint column a family admits). Pre-fix: 14/521 live families (2.69%) had a strictly-relieving singleton available and the pool contained NONE (n_w1=0, cand_best=0.000000 -- an existence hole, not a degradation); 4/19 instances (21%) affected; worst family lost relief 76.087. Post-fix (-global-k 8): capture 1.0000 on 19/19. NOT equal to P(misses the global optimum): the reference enumerates only singletons while 79% of cand's output is 2-waypoint, so L2 is unmeasured and L3 (needs the optimum itself) is not measurable at all.

headline_results.live_denominator: 725 families total; 204 (28.1%) have no relieving singleton at all (nothing to miss); 521 (71.9%) live -- the correct denominator.
headline_results.lost_best_singleton_before: 14/521 = 2.69% of live families. All 14 are TOTAL misses (cand_best = 0.000000, n_w1 = 0), not partial ones. Distinct demands = 10.
headline_results.lost_best_singleton_after: 0/521 (capture 1.0000 on 19/19 instances that have any relief; setA-18 excluded -- its hottest arc is the presolve-proven class-1 bridge, so no singleton relieves it).
headline_results.instance_level: 4/19 = 21% of instances contain at least one family that lost the best singleton: setA-04 (4 rows), setA-13 (4), setA-16 (5), setA-10 (1).
headline_results.worst_single_loss: setA-10 demand 290 slot 0: brute-force best singleton relief 76.0870, pool gave 0.0000.
headline_results.recall_is_now_circular: globalRelief selects the top-K by relief and the reference is the top-12 by relief -- the same function. global-k 8 therefore buys the top-12's first 8 MECHANICALLY: the floor is 8/12 = 66.7%, and the measured 69.0% means the strategies themselves contribute only 2.3pp. After this change recall@12 is no longer a usable strategy-quality metric, and capture = 1.0 is constructive, not evidence of quality.
headline_results.cost: 20-instance candidate time 1352 ms -> 2314 ms (+963 ms); +0.2 to +1.1 ms per family; single instance 60 families +16 ms (setA-10) to +67 ms (setA-16).
headline_results.maxw1_fragility: With global-k 8 the largest w1/family is 23 (setA-14) against MaxW1=24. cand.go:353 sorts with sort.SliceStable (relief only, no tag tie-break) and the global nodes are appended AFTER the strategy nodes (cand.go:283), so a relief tie at the cap boundary would drop a GLOBAL node and silently revert capture. Not yet triggered -- one node of headroom. Fix: raise MaxW1 by GlobalK when GlobalK>0, or front-load TagGlobal before truncation.

what_this_does_not_measure.L2_two_waypoint: The reference enumerates only singletons. 79% of cand's output is 2-waypoint and has NO counterpart, so P(the pool misses the family's truly best column) is not measurable today. This is the largest blind spot.
what_this_does_not_measure.L3_global_optimum: Would require knowing the optimum, which requires the full solve with a complete pool.
what_this_does_not_measure.snapshot: All measurements are on the EMPTY (initial) snapshot, not the mid-solve states the solver actually visits. cmd/candbench already supports -sol for that; not done here.
what_this_does_not_measure.mip_conversion: Whether the restored columns actually improve the final objective is an end-to-end question. cmd/candbench deliberately contains no MIP and cannot answer it.

suggestions_ranked: Make -cand-global-k 8 the default, but first run a targeted full-solve A/B on the four instances where the hole was real (setA-04/10/13/16), paired and repeated >=3x, because the outer loop's Gurobi spread is ~7.7% (measured in _03).

Build a 2-waypoint brute-force reference on the small instances (n<=50: setA-01/02/03/04) -- C(n-2,2) real routings -- to close the L2 blind spot. Without it the next strategy version has no comparable ruler.
Fix the MaxW1 truncation fragility (raise the cap by GlobalK, or exempt TagGlobal candidates).

The next lever is PAIR generation, not hop-ball radius: global-k already repaired the singleton side (setA-15 recall 3.1% -> 65.6%), and the ball now only gates pairing material via hot_center's offload test.

Consider offering the global nodes as pairing material too (currently deliberately excluded to control MIP size) -- 'best singleton + one detour node' is exactly the combination that unloads two arcs at once.
Do not spend further performance budget on the hop cache (BFS was never the bottleneck; _03 section 3).
